transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah… so, I’m here because at work I keep, like, leaving my station when I’m supposed to stay there. Or in meetings I’ll just pop up out of my chair before I even realize I’m doing it. My supervisor said it’s turning into a safety problem, because I kind of just take off without thinking.

It’s weird because I don’t mean to cause trouble, I just—like, one second I’m there and then I’m already moving. And then someone’s looking at me like, “Why are you over there?” So… yeah, that’s what made me come in.
Have you noticed yourself moving around or acting impulsively in other situations, like at home or with friends, or does this only happen at work?

Yeah, it’s not just like me trying to be difficult at work. It’s more like when I have to stand still by the machine, or sit through training, I get this pressure building up in my body, like I can feel it in my legs and chest almost, and I just need to move right then.

Like I’ll pace, or stretch, or suddenly feel like I have to go do something. Even if nothing’s really happening, my body feels like it can’t stay put. Training is bad because everyone’s just sitting there and I’m trying to look normal, but inside I’m like, okay, I need to get up now.
Did you experience similar feelings of restlessness or difficulty staying still when you were younger, like in school or during activities?

Yeah… yeah, definitely. Like, even in elementary school I was that kid who just could not stay in my seat. I’d be up walking around the room, or turning around talking to somebody, and the teacher would be like, “Sit down,” and I’d sit for maybe two seconds and then—yeah.

I remember getting those notes sent home, like, for blurting stuff out or talking over the teacher. My mom would get so annoyed because it was always the same thing, and I’d be like, “I wasn’t trying to be bad,” you know? I just… I’d already said it before I thought about it. And sometimes I’d get distracted by, like, the pencil sharpener or someone by the door and then I’d be out of my chair. So yeah, it’s been kind of a thing since I was little.
